title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
abstract: arXiv:2611.33010v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Can a simple mirror expose the limitations of today's robotic manipulation policies? Inspired by the mirror self-recognition test in animal cognition, we investigate whether robot policies can reliably manipulate physical objects in scenes containing their reflections. We introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark built on RoboDojo that preserves task objectives, success criteria, and policy checkpoints while comparing a mirror-free baseline with single-mirror, dual-mirror, and mirrored-tabletop conditions. Across five policies spanning Vision-Language-Action models, World Action Models, and agentic policies, every mirror condition reduces aggregate success rates: averaged over the three conditions, the drop ranges from 10.8 to 56.7 percentage points across policies, and it reaches 62.5 points on the mirrored tabletop. Because a mirror is also a physical obstacle, we compare it against geometrically matched non-reflective panels; 50--88\%

translated_title: 具身AI无法通过镜子测试：一面简单的镜子如何破坏机器人策略
translated_abstract: 一面简单的镜子能否暴露当今机器人操作策略的局限性？受动物认知中镜子自我识别测试的启发，我们研究了机器人策略能否在包含自身反射的场景中可靠地操作物理物体。我们提出了RoboDojo-Mirror，这是一个基于RoboDojo构建的基准测试，它在保持任务目标、成功标准和策略检查点不变的前提下，将无镜基线与单镜、双镜和镜面桌面条件进行对比。在涵盖视觉-语言-动作模型、世界动作模型和智能体策略的五种策略上，每种镜子条件都会降低总体成功率：对三种镜子条件取平均后，各策略的下降幅度介于10.8至56.7个百分点之间，而在镜面桌面上下降幅度达到62.5个百分点。由于镜子本身也是一种物理障碍物，我们将其与几何形状匹配的非反射面板进行比较；50--88%
tldr: 该论文提出了RoboDojo-Mirror基准测试，发现即使场景中只出现一面镜子，也会使各类机器人操作策略（包括VLA模型、世界动作模型和智能体策略）的成功率大幅下降10.8至62.5个百分点，揭示了当前具身AI对镜面反射缺乏鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark showing that even a simple mirror in the scene causes diverse robot manipulation policies—including VLA models, World Action Models, and agentic policies—to drop in success rate by 10.8 to 62.5 percentage points, revealing that embodied AI lacks robustness to mirror reflections.
